correctness.rationale: The exact payoff along a finite functional-graph walk is sum prefix q-products p_j(τ-|x_i-x_j|); its no-distance component is τ(1-Q_S), with distance penalty bounded by Δqmax. Any strategy adding a missing visited voter gives at least τ pmin Q/qmax, and replacing a maximal-abstention cycle C by another T with Q_T≤Q_C yields the same strict lower bound. Hamiltonian cycles lose visited voters under any nontrivial redirection, hence strict NE. Any other functional digraph has multiple cycles or an in-tree to its sole cycle, giving a profitable deviation. Robustness bound Δ<τ pmin Q/qmax² proves exact NE set, count (n-1)!. Three-person d=(2,1,2) equivalent zero-based (1,0,1) exact inequalities b≥max(2a,(1+a)/2) follow all deviations; two persons cannot be nonspanning NE under mutual acceptance. Independently enumerated all profiles n=2,3,4 for homogeneous and heterogeneous p and exact boundary grid.

value.rationale: A global pure-Nash equilibrium classification and factorial count under a quantitative, heterogeneous-turnout robustness regime is a natural structural game-theoretic theorem.
